primitives.name: Salary Cap Constraint
primitives.verbatim_quote: The NBA has a salary cap restricting the total amount that the teams can spend on salaries.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C': 'total available salary cap (USD)', 'S_i': 'salary offered to player i (USD)'}
primitives.assumptions: Cap is fixed per team; teams cannot exceed C without exceptions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \( \sum S_i > C \), constraint becomes binding.

layer2.mapping: Models the upper bound on team spending as a deterministic constraint in GSE state transitions.

primitives.name: Free Agent Valuation
primitives.verbatim_quote: There is also consensus information available on the market valuation of free agents based on the extensive amount of data related to their skills sets.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'V_i': 'market valuation of player i (USD)', 'A_i': 'available skill attributes of player i (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Publicly known skill metrics; V_i derived from A_i via empirical regression.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When V_i is unknown to individual teams, private information creates asymmetric equilibrium.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's probabilistic valuation kernel where V_i is estimated via Bayesian inference.
layer2.telemetry: Expected utility of signing player i vs. alternative investments

primitives.name: Multiple-Choice Knapsack
primitives.verbatim_quote: This trade-off can be solved by a dynamic program based on the multiple-choice knapsack problem, which optimizes the benefit of signing a player at any particular point in the free agency period in comparison to the opportunity costs of the cap space required to do so.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'v_i': 'value of signing player i (USD)', 'w_i': 'salary cost of player i (USD)', 'x_i': 'binary selection variable (0 or 1)', 'W': 'available cap space (USD)'}
primitives.assumptions: Players are discrete choices; value and cost are known; binary selection.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When W shrinks due to prior signings, suboptimal selections may occur.

layer2.mapping: GSE uses this as core optimization engine for sequential player acquisition decisions.
layer2.telemetry: Cumulative value of signed players vs. remaining cap space

reasoning_traces.think:
The core problem is optimizing team roster construction within a fixed budget (salary cap) while accounting for uncertain private valuations of players. The model treats free agents as items in a knapsack, where capacity is the salary cap and value is derived from skill-based market valuation. The dynamic programming formulation allows teams to evaluate trade-offs between immediate gains and future flexibility. Private information asymmetry introduces uncertainty in player valuation, leading to strategic behavior such as signaling interest early. As the season progresses, the cap shrinks, reducing the effective size of the knapsack and altering the optimal selection policy. The system exhibits non-stationary dynamics due to changing player availability and evolving cap constraints. Failure modes include overcommitment to high-value players early, leaving insufficient cap room for later acquisitions, or underestimating the true value of players whose skills align with team needs.
